slides.title: VT-WAM: Visual-Tactile World Action Model for Contact-Rich Manipulation
slides.highlight: VT-WAM integrates future visual and tactile deformation predictions with action generation using a flow matching framework to improve contact-rich manipulation.

card.one_liner: VT-WAM improves contact-rich manipulation by jointly predicting future visual, tactile, and action dynamics.
card.key_idea: A flow matching framework using Asymmetric MoT Attention for visual-tactile integration and contact-gated AVTAG to prioritize tactile evidence during physical interaction phases.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on six real-world tasks; achieved 71.67% average success rate, significantly outperforming Fast-WAM (45.00%) and OmniVTLA (35.83%).
card.limitation: The model focuses on individual-task specialization; multi-task training and scaling laws remain unexplored.

slides.title: UniTacVLA: Unified Tactile Understanding and Prediction in Vision Language Action Models
slides.tldr: UNIFIED TACTILE LEARNING FOR CONTACT-RICH MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework for modeling tactile signals as dynamic interaction cues for contact understanding and prediction, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on physics/force-based skill estimation and human-AI coadaptation in assembly tasks.

card.one_liner: UniTacVLA improves contact-rich robotic manipulation by unifying tactile semantic understanding and future tactile prediction.
card.key_idea: A framework using tactile chain-of-thought reasoning and coarse-to-fine future tactile prediction to create a proactive prior for a high-frequency action-tactile mixed controller.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 8 real-world tasks (adjustment, wiping, insertion, assembly) under clean and perturbed settings; outperformed baselines like TacVLA and VTLA in success rates.
card.limitation: Susceptible to operator-dependent noise in teleoperated data and lacks explicit modeling of force/torque signals.

slides.title: Imagining the Sense of Touch: Touch-Informed Manipulation via Imagined Tactile Representations
slides.highlight: TacImag predicts tactile observations from vision and proprioception, enabling touch-informed manipulation without requiring tactile hardware at deployment.

card.one_liner: TacImag enables touch-informed robotic manipulation using only visual and proprioceptive inputs at deployment time.
card.key_idea: A conditional diffusion model predicts tactile representations (TacRGB or TacFF) from vision and proprioception, providing contact-aware supervision for a frozen, tactile-conditioned manipulation policy.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 6 simulated and 4 real-world tasks; imagined TacFF improved contact-sensitive tasks by 44.4% on average in real-world trials.
card.limitation: Effectiveness depends strongly on matching the tactile representation (RGB vs. Force Field) to the specific task requirements.

slides.title: Human-Centric Transferable Tactile Pre-Training for Dexterous Robotic Manipulation
slides.tldr: SCALABLE TACTILE PRE-TRAINING VIA HUMAN-TO-ROBOT TRANSFER
slides.highlight: This work introduces H-Tac and TTP to model contact dynamics and precise physical interactions through human-to-robot tactile transfer, supporting MOSAIC's focus on physics/force-based skill acquisition.

card.one_liner: TTP enables robotic dexterous manipulation by pre-training VLA models on large-scale human tactile-action data.
card.key_idea: A dual-expert VLA system using unified action/tactile spaces and a tactile prediction expert to transfer human contact dynamics to robots via a manifold-preserving gating mechanism.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on LIBERO, RoboCasa simulations and 9 real-robot tasks (e.g., peeling, chip picking) across various arms and hands; showed superior fine-grained manipulation.

slides.title: RoboTacDex: A Dexterous Visual-Tactile-Action Dataset for Humanoid Manipulation
slides.highlight: This dataset provides multi-modal trajectories of dexterous humanoid manipulation, supporting RwB's focus on embodied AI and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: RoboTacDex is a large-scale multi-modal dataset for humanoid dexterous manipulation using the Unitree G1 robot.
card.key_idea: 6k trajectories across 19 tasks and 22 objects, featuring multi-view RGB-D, tactile feedback, and semantic annotations for dual-arm dexterous manipulation.
card.evaluation: Three imitation learning models were tested; results showed successful trials and moderate generalization across various task categories.

slides.title: Guided Action Flow: Q-Guided Inference for Flow-Matching Vision-Language-Action Policies
slides.highlight: This framework uses a learned action-chunk critic to guide the reverse-time flow sampler of a frozen SmolVLA policy, improving success rates on LIBERO manipulation tasks without retraining the base model.

card.one_liner: Guided Action Flow improves frozen flow-matching VLA policies using an inference-time critic to guide action generation.
card.key_idea: A learned action-chunk critic provides value gradients during the reverse-time flow sampling of a frozen SmolVLA policy, using an ensemble disagreement gate to manage uncertainty.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on LIBERO tasks; single-task success rose from 68% to 82%. Multi-family validation improved by 10pp, though held-out gains were modest (+2.5pp).
card.limitation: Critic generalization is a bottleneck; performance is sensitive to hyperparameters and the critic can produce harmful gradients on unseen tasks.

slides.title: From Grasps to Dexterity: Large-Scale Grasp Pretraining for Dexterous Manipulation
slides.tldr: GRASP PRETRAINING FOR DEXTEROUS TOOL USE
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that large-scale grasp datasets can be used to pretrain low-level controllers for contact-rich dexterous manipulation and articulated tool use. The approach outperforms end-to-end diffusion policies in both simulation and real-world tasks.

card.one_liner: Large-scale grasp datasets can pretrain low-level controllers for complex, articulated dexterous tool-use tasks.
card.key_idea: A hierarchical imitation learning framework combining high-level 16-keypoint sub-goal prediction with a low-level controller pretrained on G2D-Pretrain (355k trajectories augmented from Dexonomy).
card.evaluation: Evaluated on DexCraft (6 simulation tasks) and 3 real-world tasks; outperformed DP3 and HP-Scratch, improving real-world success by 33.3 percentage points.
card.limitation: Relies on manually labeled sub-goals for the hierarchical framework and uses single object instances per task.

slides.title: Embodied.cpp: A Portable Inference Runtime of Embodied AI Models on Heterogeneous Robots
slides.tldr: PORTABLE C++ INFERENCE RUNTIME FOR EMBODIED AI
slides.highlight: Embodied.cpp provides a portable C++ runtime for VLA and WAM models, enabling efficient closed-loop execution and multi-rate inference on heterogeneous robots. This supports RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated interaction by streamlining model deployment on edge devices.

card.one_liner: Embodied.cpp is a portable C++ inference runtime for deploying VLA and WAM models on heterogeneous robots.
card.key_idea: A five-layer architecture (input adapters, sequence builders, backbone execution, head plugins, deployment adapters) supporting multi-rate execution and latency-first batch-1 inference across diverse edge hardware.
card.evaluation: Tested on HY-VLA (100% success) and pi0.5 (91% success) VLA models, plus a LingBot-VA WAM block reducing memory from 312.2 to 88.1 MiB.
card.limitation: Full closed-loop WAM results are not yet available due to instability on constrained local edge devices.
